observation: Production replay requires externally grounded session closes. Original Yahoo daily bars provide session openings, not observed trade or vendor-availability timestamps. Prior source admission was incomplete.
hypothesized_cause: The prior engineering fixtures did not establish a complete historical session clock for the real pre-2017 sources.
change: Prospectively use exact 2005-2016 session opens and scheduled closes extracted from the pinned exchange_calendars XNYS resource, subject to exact equality of all asset session dates and source-opening timestamps. This is a scheduled exchange clock convention within retrospective development, not a claim of observed execution latency or historical point-in-time data availability.
limitations: Community-maintained historical schedule, not exchange-issued certification of every row
Scheduled quotes and decision/fill offsets, not observed execution or source latency
Current-vintage retrospective data, not point-in-time confirmation
Cash dividends on ex-date remain the declared convention, not payment-date settlement
predicted_effect: Makes calendar completeness and session timing falsifiable before consumed research execution; no predicted improvement in model scores or wealth.
discriminating_experiment: Metadata-only exact source/calendar/date/timestamp matching plus adversarial missing-session, early-close, corruption, decision-identity and scope tests; numerical source preparation only after the separate consumption and resource gates.
